p0.original: (This appendix should be consulted after first reading Welcome to Economics!) Economics is not math. There is no important concept in this course that cannot be explained without mathematics. That said, math is a tool that can be used to illustrate economic concepts. Remember the saying a picture is worth a thousand words? Instead of a picture, think of a graph. It is the same thing. Economists use models as the primary tool to derive insights about economic issues and problems. Math is one way of working with (or manipulating) economic models.
p0.zh: (此附录在一读后应参考) 欢迎加入经济学!) 经济学不是数学. 在这个课程中没有任何重要的概念,没有数学是无法解释的. 尽管如此,数学是一个工具,可以用来说明经济概念。还记得这句谚语吗? 一张画值一千字?而不是图片,想一想图。 这是同样的事情。经济学家将模型作为了解经济问题的主要工具。数学是与(或操纵)经济模型合作的一种方式.

p1.original: There are other ways of representing models, such as text or narrative. But why would you use your fist to bang a nail, if you had a hammer? Math has certain advantages over text. It disciplines your thinking by making you specify exactly what you mean. You can get away with fuzzy thinking in your head, but you cannot when you reduce a model to algebraic equations. At the same time, math also has disadvantages. Mathematical models are necessarily based on simplifying assumptions, so they are not likely to be perfectly realistic. Mathematical models also lack the nuances which can be found in narrative models. The point is that math is one tool, but it is not the only tool or even always the best tool economists can use. So what math will you need for this book? The answer is: little more than high school algebra and graphs. You will need to know:
p1.zh: 还有其它代表模型的方法,如文字或叙事. 但如果你有锤子,你为什么要用拳头敲钉子?数学比文字有一定优势. 它约束你的思考, 让你精确地说明你的意思。头脑中模糊的思维可以逃脱,但当你将模型降低到代数方程时却无法逃脱. 同时,数学也有缺点.数学模型必然基于简化的假设,因此它们不太可能是完全现实的.数学模型也缺乏在叙事模型中可以找到的细微差别.关键在于数学是一个工具,但它不是唯一的工具,甚至总是经济学家能够使用的最佳工具.这本书你需要什么数学?答案是:小于高中代数和图表. 你将需要知道:

p7.original: In this text, we will use the easiest math possible, and we will introduce it in this appendix. So if you find some math in the book that you cannot follow, come back to this appendix to review. Like most things, math has diminishing returns. A little math ability goes a long way; the more advanced math you bring in, the less additional knowledge that will get you. That said, if you are going to major in economics, you should consider learning a little calculus. It will be worth your while in terms of helping you learn advanced economics more quickly.
p7.zh: 在这个文本中,我们将使用尽可能简单的数学,我们将在本附录中介绍。 所以如果你在书里找到一些你无法遵循的数学, 请回到本附录来审查。和大多数东西一样,数学的回报率在下降.一点点的数学能力可以走很长的路; 你带来的数学越先进, 得到的知识就越少。也就是说,如果你要攻读经济学专业, 你应该考虑学习一点微积分。帮助你更快地学习先进的经济学,这值得你花时间。

p9.original: Often economic models (or parts of models) are expressed in terms of mathematical functions. What is a function? A function describes a relationship. Sometimes the relationship is a definition. For example (using words), your professor is Adam Smith. This could be expressed as Professor = Adam Smith. Or Friends = Bob + Shawn + Margaret.
p9.zh: 经济模型(或模型的一部分)往往用数学函数来表示. 什么是职能? 一个函数描述一种关系. 有时,这种关系是一个定义. 例如(使用单词),你的教授是亚当·斯密. 这可以表示为教授=亚当·斯密. 或者朋友=鲍勃+肖恩+玛格丽特.

p10.original: Often in economics, functions describe cause and effect. The variable on the left-hand side is what is being explained (“the effect”). On the right-hand side is what is doing the explaining (“the causes”). For example, suppose your GPA was determined as follows:
p10.zh: 在经济学中,函数往往描述因果关系。左侧的变量是正在解释的内容(“效果”)。右边是解释的原因。 例如,假设您的GPA是按以下方式确定的:

p11.original: This equation states that your GPA depends on three things: your combined SAT score, your class attendance, and the number of hours you spend studying. It also says that study time is twice as important (0.50) as either combined_SAT score (0.25) or class_attendance (0.25). If this relationship is true, how could you raise your GPA? By not skipping class and studying more. Note that you cannot do anything about your SAT score, since if you are in college, you have (presumably) already taken the SATs.
p11.zh: 这个方程表示您的 GPA 取决于三件事: 合并的SAT分数,你的班级出勤率, 以及你学习的小时数。 它还说,学习时间比综合_SAT得分(0.25)或班级_考勤(0.25)重要一倍(0.50)。 如果这种关系是真的,你怎么能提高你的GPA? 不跳过课和学习更多。请注意,你无法对SAT分数做任何事情,因为如果你在大学,你(大概)已经接受了SAT分数。

p12.original: Of course, economic models express relationships using economic variables, like Budget = money_spent_on_econ_books + money_spent_on_music, assuming that the only things you buy are economics books and music.
p12.zh: 当然,经济模型用经济变量来表达关系,比如预算=money_spent_on_econ_books+money_spent_on_music,假设你购买的只有经济学书籍和音乐.

p35.original: Slope and the Algebra of Straight Lines

p36.original: This example illustrates how the b and m terms in an equation for a straight line determine the shape of the line. The b term is called the y-intercept. The reason for this name is that, if x = 0, then the b term will reveal where the line intercepts, or crosses, the y-axis. In this example, the line hits the vertical axis at 9. The m term in the equation for the line is the slope. Remember that slope is defined as rise over run; more specifically, the slope of a line from one point to another is the change in the vertical axis divided by the change in the horizontal axis. In this example, each time the x term increases by one (the run), the y term rises by three. Thus, the slope of this line is three. Specifying a y-intercept and a slope—that is, specifying b and m in the equation for a line—will identify a specific line. Although it is rare for real-world data points to arrange themselves as an exact straight line, it often turns out that a straight line can offer a reasonable approximation of actual data.
p36.zh: 这个例子说明了直线方程中的b和m术语如何决定直线的形状.b术语称为y-intercept. 这个名称的理由是,如果x=0,那么b术语将揭示线截击,或交叉Y轴的位置. 在这个例子中,线在9点击中垂直轴.线条方程中的m术语是斜线.记住,坡度被定义为在运行中上升;更具体地说,一线从一个点到另一个点的坡度是垂直轴的改变,除以水平轴的改变. 在这个例子中,每逢x名词增加一个(运行),y名词增加三个. 因此,这条线的坡度是三.指定一个y-截面和一个斜面,即指定一条线的公式中的b和m,将确定一条特定的线。 虽然现实世界的数据点很少将自己安排成精确的直线,但往往发现直线可以提供合理的实际数据的近似值.

p38.original: The concept of slope is very useful in economics, because it measures the relationship between two variables. A positive slope means that two variables are positively related; that is, when x increases, so does y, or when x decreases, y decreases also. Graphically, a positive slope means that as a line on the line graph moves from left to right, the line rises. The length-weight relationship, shown in  later in this Appendix, has a positive slope. We will learn in other chapters that price and quantity supplied have a positive relationship; that is, firms will supply more when the price is higher.
p38.zh: 坡度的概念在经济学中非常有用,因为它衡量两个变量之间的关系. 正斜率表示两个变量是正相关联的;也就是说,当x增加时,y也增加,或者当x减少时,y也减少.图形上,正坡是指随着线图上的一条线从左向右移动,线条上升. 本附录后面部分显示的长度-加权关系具有正斜率. 我们将在其他章节中了解到,供应的价格和数量有着积极的关系;也就是说,当价格较高时,公司将提供更多的供应。

p39.original: A negative slope means that two variables are negatively related; that is, when x increases, y decreases, or when x decreases, y increases. Graphically, a negative slope means that, as the line on the line graph moves from left to right, the line falls. The altitude-air density relationship, shown in  later in this appendix, has a negative slope. We will learn that price and quantity demanded have a negative relationship; that is, consumers will purchase less when the price is higher.
p39.zh: 负斜率意味着两个变量是负相关联的;即当x增加,y减少,或x减少,y增加.图形上,负斜坡意味着,随着线图上的线从左向右移动,线会下降. 本附录后面部分显示的高度-空气密度关系具有负斜坡. 我们将了解到,所要求的价格和数量有负面关系;也就是说,当价格较高时,消费者将减少购买。

p40.original: A slope of zero means that there is no relationship between x and y. Graphically, the line is flat; that is, zero rise over the run.  of the unemployment rate, shown later in this appendix, illustrates a common pattern of many line graphs: some segments where the slope is positive, other segments where the slope is negative, and still other segments where the slope is close to zero.
p40.zh: 0的坡度意味着x和y之间没有关系. 从图形上看,该线是平的;也就是说,本附录后面显示的失业率零上升。 它显示了许多线图的共同规律:坡度为正的段,坡度为负的段,坡度接近于零的其他段。

p41.original: The slope of a straight line between two points can be calculated in numerical terms. To calculate slope, begin by designating one point as the “starting point” and the other point as the “end point” and then calculating the rise over run between these two points. As an example, consider the slope of the air density graph between the points representing an altitude of 4,000 meters and an altitude of 6,000 meters:
p41.zh: 两个点之间的直线的坡度可以用数字计算. 为了计算坡度,首先指定一个点为“起始点”,另一个点为“终点”,然后计算这两个点之间的上升。 例如,考虑代表4 000米高度和6 000米高度的点之间的空气密度图的坡度:

p42.original: Rise: Change in variable on vertical axis (end point minus original point)
p42.zh: 升起: 垂直轴上的变量变化( 结束点减原点)

p43.original: Run: Change in variable on horizontal axis (end point minus original point)
p43.zh: 运行: 水平轴上的变量变化( 结束点减去原点)

p44.original: Thus, the slope of a straight line between these two points would be that from the altitude of 4,000 meters up to 6,000 meters, the density of the air decreases by approximately 0.1 kilograms/cubic meter for each of the next 1,000 meters.
p44.zh: 因此,这两个点之间直线的坡度将是从4000米高度到6000米,空气密度在接下来的1000米中,每座下降约0.1公斤/立方厘米.

p45.original: Suppose the slope of a line were to increase. Graphically, that means it would get steeper. Suppose the slope of a line were to decrease. Then it would get flatter. These conditions are true whether or not the slope was positive or negative to begin with. A higher positive slope means a steeper upward tilt to the line, while a smaller positive slope means a flatter upward tilt to the line. A negative slope that is larger in absolute value (that is, more negative) means a steeper downward tilt to the line. A slope of zero is a horizontal flat line. A vertical line has an infinite slope.
p45.zh: 假设一条线的坡度会增加。 从图形上看,这意味着它会变得更加陡峭。假设一线的坡度会降低. 然后它会得到恭维。不论坡度是正的还是负的,这些条件都是真实的。较高的正坡表示向线向上倾斜较陡,而较小的正坡表示向线向上倾斜.绝对值较大的负斜率(即更负的斜率)是指向线向下倾斜的更陡的斜率.零坡为水平平线.垂直线有无限的坡度.

p46.original: Suppose a line has a larger intercept. Graphically, that means it would shift out (or up) from the old origin, parallel to the old line. If a line has a smaller intercept, it would shift in (or down), parallel to the old line.
p46.zh: 如果一线有更大的截击。 从图形上看,这意味着它会从旧起源中向外转移(或向上),与旧线平行. 如果一线有较小的截击,则会与旧线平行在(或向下)转移.

p48.original: Economists often use models to answer a specific question, like: What will the unemployment rate be if the economy grows at 3% per year? Answering specific questions requires solving the “system” of equations that represent the model.
p48.zh: 经济学家们经常用模型来回答一个具体问题,比如:如果经济以每年3%的速度增长,失业率会是怎样的?回答具体问题需要解决代表模型的方程式的“系统”。

p63.original: We will use graphs more frequently in this book than algebra, but now you know the math behind the graphs.
p63.zh: 我们将更频繁地使用图表 在这本书中比代数, 但是现在你知道图表背后的数学。

p65.original: Growth rates are frequently encountered in real world economics. A growth rate is simply the percentage change in some quantity. It could be your income. It could be a business’s sales. It could be a nation’s GDP. The formula for computing a growth rate is straightforward:
p65.zh: 在现实世界经济中经常遇到增长率问题。增长率只是某些数量的百分比变化。这可能是你的收入。这可能是企业的销售。这可能是一个国家的国内生产总值。计算增长率的公式很简单:

p66.original: Suppose your job pays $10 per hour. Your boss, however, is so impressed with your work that he gives you a $2 per hour raise. The percentage change (or growth rate) in your pay is $2/$10 = 0.20 or 20%.
p66.zh: 假设你的工作每小时要付10美元 不过你老板对你的工作印象深刻 他给你每小时两块钱工资的百分比变化(或增长率)为每10美元2美元=0.20美元或20%。

p67.original: To compute the growth rate for data over an extended period of time, for example, the average annual growth in GDP over a decade or more, the denominator is commonly defined a little differently. In the previous example, we defined the quantity as the initial quantity—or the quantity when we started. This is fine for a one-time calculation, but when we compute the growth over and over, it makes more sense to define the quantity as the average quantity over the period in question, which is defined as the quantity halfway between the initial quantity and the next quantity. This is harder to explain in words than to show with an example. Suppose a nation’s GDP was $1 trillion in 2005 and $1.03 trillion in 2006. The growth rate between 2005 and 2006 would be the change in GDP ($1.03 trillion – $1.00 trillion) divided by the average GDP between 2005 and 2006 ($1.03 trillion + $1.00 trillion)/2. In other words:
p67.zh: 为了计算长时间内的数据增长率,例如,十年或更长时间内国内生产总值的年均增长率,通常对分母的定义略有不同。 在前一个例子中,我们把数量定义为初始数量——或我们开始时的数量。 这对一次性计算来说是好的,但当我们计算一次和多次的增长时,将数量定义为相关期间的平均数量更有意义,因为平均数量被定义为初始数量与下一个数量之间的中间数量. 这比举个例子更难用言语解释。 如果一个国家的国内生产总值在2005年为1万亿美元,在2006年为1.03万亿美元。2005年至2006年的增长率是国内生产总值的变化(1.03万亿美元,1.0万亿美元),除以2005年至2006年的平均国内生产总值(1.03万亿美元+1.0万亿美元)/2。换句话说:

p68.original: Note that if we used the first method, the calculation would be ($1.03 trillion – $1.00 trillion) / $1.00 trillion = 3% growth, which is approximately the same as the second, more complicated method. If you need a rough approximation, use the first method. If you need accuracy, use the second method.
p68.zh: 请注意,如果我们使用第一种方法,计算结果将是(1.03万亿—1.0万亿) / 1.0万亿=3%的增长,这与第二种方法大致相同,更为复杂。 如果需要粗略的近似,请使用第一种方法.需要精度的,使用第二种方法.

p69.original: A few things to remember: A positive growth rate means the quantity is growing. A smaller growth rate means the quantity is growing more slowly. A larger growth rate means the quantity is growing more quickly. A negative growth rate means the quantity is decreasing.
p69.zh: 几件事要记住:正增长率意味着数量在增长。较低的增长率意味着数量增长较慢。较大的增长率意味着数量增长更快。负增长率意味着数量正在减少。

p70.original: The same change over times yields a smaller growth rate. If you got a $2 raise each year, in the first year the growth rate would be $2/$10 = 20%, as shown above. But in the second year, the growth rate would be $2/$12 = 0.167 or 16.7% growth. In the third year, the same $2 raise would correspond to a $2/$14 = 14.2%. The moral of the story is this: To keep the growth rate the same, the change must increase each period.
p70.zh: 随着时间的推移,同样的变化产生较小的增长率。 如果你每年加薪2美元,第一年的增长率为2美元/10美元=20%,如上所示。 但在第二年,增长率将为2美元/12美元=0.167美元或16.7%。 在第三年,同样增加的2美元相当于2美元/14美元=14.2%。故事的道德是:为了保持增长率不变,必须增加每个时期的变化.

p71.original: Displaying Data Graphically and Interpreting the Graph
p71.zh: 以图形方式显示数据并解释图表

p72.original: Graphs are also used to display data or evidence. Graphs are a method of presenting numerical patterns. They condense detailed numerical information into a visual form in which relationships and numerical patterns can be seen more easily. For example, which countries have larger or smaller populations? A careful reader could examine a long list of numbers representing the populations of many countries, but with over 200 nations in the world, searching through such a list would take concentration and time. Putting these same numbers on a graph can quickly reveal population patterns. Economists use graphs both for a compact and readable presentation of groups of numbers and for building an intuitive grasp of relationships and connections.
p72.zh: 图表也用于显示数据或证据。图表是显示数字模式的一种方法。 它们将详细的数字信息压缩成一种视觉形式,在这种形式中,关系和数字模式可以更容易地看到. 例如,哪些国家的人口较多或较少? 一个仔细的读者可以审查一个代表许多国家人口的长长的数字清单,但是,如果世界上有200多个国家,那么通过这样一个清单来寻找需要集中和时间。把这些相同的数字放在图表上,可以很快揭示出人口形态.经济学家既使用图表,也使用图表,对数字组进行紧凑和可读的表述,并直观地掌握关系和联系。

p73.original: Three types of graphs are used in this book: line graphs, pie graphs, and bar graphs. Each is discussed below. We also provide warnings about how graphs can be manipulated to alter viewers’ perceptions of the relationships in the data.
p73.zh: 本书使用三种类型的图案:行图,派图,和条图. 下文将讨论每个问题。 我们还警告如何操纵图表来改变观众对数据中关系的看法。

p75.original: The graphs we have discussed so far are called line graphs, because they show a relationship between two variables: one measured on the horizontal axis and the other measured on the vertical axis.
p75.zh: 迄今我们讨论的图表被称为线图,因为它们显示了两个变量之间的关系:一个在水平轴上测量,另一个在垂直轴上测量.

p76.original: Sometimes it is useful to show more than one set of data on the same axes. The data in  is displayed in  which shows the relationship between two variables: length and median weight for American baby boys and girls during the first three years of life. (The median means that half of all babies weigh more than this and half weigh less.) The line graph measures length in inches on the horizontal axis and weight in pounds on the vertical axis. For example, point A on the figure shows that a boy who is 28 inches long will have a median weight of about 19 pounds. One line on the graph shows the length-weight relationship for boys and the other line shows the relationship for girls. This kind of graph is widely used by healthcare providers to check whether a child’s physical development is roughly on track.
p76.zh: 有时在同一个轴上显示不止一组数据是有用的.所显示的数据显示了两个变量之间的关系:美国婴儿出生前三年的长度和体重中位数。(中位数表示所有婴儿中一半的体重超过这个,一半的体重更小. )线形图在水平轴上以英寸表示长度,在垂直轴上以磅表示重量. 例如,图上的A点显示,一个身长28英寸的男孩的中位体重会达到约19磅. 图中的一行显示男孩的体重长度关系,另一行显示女孩的关系。 这种图表被医疗保健机构广泛用于检查儿童的身体发育是否大致正常。

p77.original: The Length-Weight Relationship for American Boys and Girls
p77.zh: 美国男孩和女孩的长度-体重关系

p78.original: Length to Weight Relationship for American Boys and Girls
p78.zh: 美国男女儿童体重关系的长度

p125.original: Not all relationships in economics are linear. Sometimes they are curves.  presents another example of a line graph, representing the data from . In this case, the line graph shows how thin the air becomes when you climb a mountain. The horizontal axis of the figure shows altitude, measured in meters above sea level. The vertical axis measures the density of the air at each altitude. Air density is measured by the weight of the air in a cubic meter of space (that is, a box measuring one meter in height, width, and depth). As the graph shows, air pressure is heaviest at ground level and becomes lighter as you climb.  shows that a cubic meter of air at an altitude of 500 meters weighs approximately one kilogram (about 2.2 pounds). However, as the altitude increases, air density decreases. A cubic meter of air at the top of Mount Everest, at about 8,828 meters, would weigh only 0.023 kilograms. The thin air at high altitudes explains why many mountain climbers need to use oxygen tanks as they reach the top of a mountain.
p125.zh: 并不是经济学中的所有关系都是线性的. 有时它们是曲线。呈现出一个行图的另一个例子,代表来自 . 在这种情况下,线性图表显示,在攀登一座山时,空气会变得多么稀薄. 图中的水平轴显示海拔高度,以海拔米数衡量.垂直轴测量每个高度的空气密度.空气密度以空气在立方公尺空间(即一个以高度、宽度和深度衡量一个公尺的盒子)中的重量来衡量。 如图所示,气压在地面水平上最重,在攀登时会变得轻一些. 显示500米高度的立方体空气重约1公斤(约2.2磅). 然而,随着高度的提高,空气密度下降.珠穆朗玛峰顶部的一块立方体空气,高度约8,828米,重量仅为0.023公斤.高空的薄空气解释了为什么许多登山者在到达山顶时需要使用氧气罐.

p126.zh: 高度- 空气密度关系

p127.zh: 高度与空气密度的关系

p129.zh: 空气密度(千克/立方公尺)

p172.original: The length-weight relationship and the altitude-air density relationships in these two figures represent averages. If you were to collect actual data on air pressure at different altitudes, the same altitude in different geographic locations will have slightly different air density, depending on factors like how far you are from the equator, local weather conditions, and the humidity in the air. Similarly, in measuring the height and weight of children for the previous line graph, children of a particular height would have a range of different weights, some above average and some below. In the real world, this sort of variation in data is common. The task of a researcher is to organize that data in a way that helps to understand typical patterns. The study of statistics, especially when combined with computer statistics and spreadsheet programs, is a great help in organizing this kind of data, plotting line graphs, and looking for typical underlying relationships. For most economics and social science majors, a statistics course will be required at some point.
p172.zh: 这两个数字中的长度-加权关系和高度-空气密度关系代表平均值. 如果收集不同高度的气压实际数据,不同地理位置的相同高度的空气密度会略有不同,这取决于你距离赤道多远,当地天气条件,空气湿度等因素. 同样,在为上一个行图衡量儿童身高和体重时,某一特定高度的儿童会有不同的权重范围,有些高于平均水平,有些低于平均水平。 在现实世界中,这种数据变化是常见的.研究者的任务是以有助于理解典型规律的方式整理这些数据.统计学的研究,特别是结合计算机统计和电子表格程序的研究,对于整理这类数据,绘制行图,寻找典型的内在关系,是大有帮助的. 对于大多数经济学和社会学专业,在某个时候需要开设统计课程.

p173.original: One common line graph is called a time series, in which the horizontal axis shows time and the vertical axis displays another variable. Thus, a time series graph shows how a variable changes over time.  shows the unemployment rate in the United States since 1975, where unemployment is defined as the percentage of adults who want jobs and are looking for a job, but cannot find one. The points for the unemployment rate in each year are plotted on the graph, and a line then connects the points, showing how the unemployment rate has moved up and down since 1975. The line graph makes it easy to see, for example, that the highest unemployment rate during this time period was slightly less than 10% in the early 1980s and 2010, while the unemployment rate declined from the early 1990s to the end of the 1990s, before rising and then falling back in the early 2000s, and then rising sharply during the recession from 2008–2009.
p173.zh: 一个常见的线形图称为时间序列,其中水平轴显示时间,垂直轴显示另一个变量. 因此,一个时间序列图显示一个变量如何随时间而变化. 1975年以来美国的失业率被定义为希望工作并寻找工作但找不到工作的成年人的百分比. 每年失业率的点数在图上绘制,然后用一条线连接点数,显示失业率自1975年以来如何上下移动. 例如,行图很容易看出,这一时期最高的失业率在1980年代初和2010年略低于10%,而失业率从1990年代初到1990年代末有所下降,在2000年代初上升后又回落,然后在2008-2009年衰退期间急剧上升。

p176.original: A pie graph (sometimes called a pie chart) is used to show how an overall total is divided into parts. A circle represents a group as a whole. The slices of this circular “pie” show the relative sizes of subgroups.
p176.zh: 馅饼图(有时也叫馅饼图),用来显示一个总体总数如何被分成几个部分. 一个圆形代表一个整体的团体. 这一循环“皮”的片段显示了分组的相对规模。

p177.original: shows how the U.S. population was divided among children, working age adults, and the elderly in 1970, 2000, and what is projected for 2030. The information is first conveyed with numbers in , and then in three pie charts. The first column of  shows the total U.S. population for each of the three years. Columns 2–4 categorize the total in terms of age groups—from birth to 18 years, from 19 to 64 years, and 65 years and above. In columns 2–4, the first number shows the actual number of people in each age category, while the number in parentheses shows the percentage of the total population comprised by that age group.
p177.zh: 说明1970年、2000年美国人口如何在儿童、工作年龄成年人和老年人之间划分,以及2030年的预测。信息首先以数字在.,然后用三个馅饼图来传递。 第一栏列出美国三年中每年的人口总数. 第2至第4栏按年龄组对总数进行了分类,从出生到18岁,从19岁至64岁,以及65岁及以上。 在第2至第4栏中,第一个数字显示每个年龄组中的实际人数,而括号中的数字显示该年龄组占总人口的百分比。

p178.zh: 美国.1970年、2000年和2030年年龄分布(预测)

p199.original: Pie Graphs of the U.S. Age Distribution (numbers in millions)
p199.zh: 美国的派图.年龄分布(单位:百万)

p200.original: In a pie graph, each slice of the pie represents a share of the total, or a percentage. For example, 50% would be half of the pie and 20% would be one-fifth of the pie. The three pie graphs in  show that the share of the U.S. population 65 and over is growing. The pie graphs allow you to get a feel for the relative size of the different age groups from 1970 to 2000 to 2030, without requiring you to slog through the specific numbers and percentages in the table. Some common examples of how pie graphs are used include dividing the population into groups by age, income level, ethnicity, religion, occupation; dividing different firms into categories by size, industry, number of employees; and dividing up government spending or taxes into its main categories.
p200.zh: 在馅饼图中,每片馅饼代表了总量的一定份额,或百分比. 例如,50%是派的一半,20%是派的五分之一。三个派图显示,美国65岁及以上人口的比例正在增加。派图可以让你对1970年至2000年到2030年不同年龄组的相对大小有感觉,而不需要你通过表中的具体数字和百分比来表示.使用派图的一些常见例子包括按年龄、收入水平、族裔、宗教、职业将人口分为几类;按规模、行业、雇员人数将不同的公司分为几类;将政府开支或税收分为主要类别。

p202.original: A bar graph uses the height of different bars to compare quantities.  lists the 12 most populous countries in the world.  provides this same data in a bar graph. The height of the bars corresponds to the population of each country. Although you may know that China and India are the most populous countries in the world, seeing how the bars on the graph tower over the other countries helps illustrate the magnitude of the difference between the sizes of national populations.
p202.zh: 条形图使用不同条的高度来比较数量. 列出世界上人口最多的12个国家. 在条形图中提供同样的数据.栏杆的高度与每个国家的人口相对应. 尽管你们可能知道中国和印度是世界上人口最多的国家,但看到图塔上横跨其他国家的栏杆如何有助于说明各国人口规模之间的差别。

p203.original: Leading Countries of the World by Population, 2015 (in millions)
p203.zh: 2015年按人口分列的世界主要国家(百万)

p204.original: Leading 12 Countries of the World by Population
p204.zh: 按人口分列的12个世界领先国家

p231.original: Bar graphs can be subdivided in a way that reveals information similar to that we can get from pie charts.  offers three bar graphs based on the information from  about the U.S. age distribution in 1970, 2000, and 2030.  (a) shows three bars for each year, representing the total number of persons in each age bracket for each year.  (b) shows just one bar for each year, but the different age groups are now shaded inside the bar. In  (c), still based on the same data, the vertical axis measures percentages rather than the number of persons. In this case, all three bar graphs are the same height, representing 100% of the population, with each bar divided according to the percentage of population in each age group. It is sometimes easier for a reader to run their eyes across several bar graphs, comparing the shaded areas, rather than trying to compare several pie graphs.
p231.zh: 条形图可以被细分为揭示出类似我们从馅饼图中获得的信息. 提供基于1970年,2000年和2030年美国年龄分布信息的三个条形图.(a) 每年显示三个栏,代表每年每个年龄段的总人数。(b) 每年只显示一个栏目,但不同的年龄组现在在栏目内遮蔽。 在(c)项中,纵向轴线仍然根据同一数据衡量百分比,而不是人数。 在这种情况下,所有三个条形图都是相同的高度,代表了人口的100%,每个条形图都按照每个年龄组的人口百分比进行划分.读者有时比较容易将眼睛横穿几个条形图,比较阴影区域,而不是试图比较几个饼形图.

p233.original: and  show how the bars can represent countries or years, and how the vertical axis can represent a numerical or a percentage value. Bar graphs can also compare size, quantity, rates, distances, and other quantitative categories.
p233.zh: ,并显示条可以如何代表国家或年份,垂直轴可以如何代表一个数值或百分比值。条形图还可以比较大小,数量,速率,距离,以及其他数量类别.

p234.original: Comparing Line Graphs with Pie Charts and Bar Graphs
p234.zh: 将行图与比图和条图进行比较

p235.original: Now that you are familiar with pie graphs, bar graphs, and line graphs, how do you know which graph to use for your data? Pie graphs are often better than line graphs at showing how an overall group is divided. However, if a pie graph has too many slices, it can become difficult to interpret.
p235.zh: 现在,你熟悉派图,条图,线图, 你怎么知道哪一个图可以用于你的数据?派图在显示一个整体组的划分方式时,往往比行图要好. 然而,如果馅饼图有太多的切片,则会变得难以解释.

p236.original: Bar graphs are especially useful when comparing quantities. For example, if you are studying the populations of different countries, as in , bar graphs can show the relationships between the population sizes of multiple countries. Not only can it show these relationships, but it can also show breakdowns of different groups within the population.
p236.zh: 在比较数量时,条形图特别有用。 例如,如果研究不同国家的人口,例如,条形图可以显示多国人口规模之间的关系。 它不仅能够显示这些关系,而且能够显示人口内部不同群体的分解.

p237.original: A line graph is often the most effective format for illustrating a relationship between two variables that are both changing. For example, time series graphs can show patterns as time changes, like the unemployment rate over time. Line graphs are widely used in economics to present continuous data about prices, wages, quantities bought and sold, the size of the economy.
p237.zh: 一个行图往往是说明两个变量之间关系的最有效的格式,两者都在变化. 例如,时间序列图可以显示随着时间变化的规律,比如随着时间推移的失业率.线形图在经济学中被广泛用于介绍有关价格,工资,买卖数量,经济规模的连续数据.

p239.original: Graphs not only reveal patterns; they can also alter how patterns are perceived. To see some of the ways this can be done, consider the line graphs of , , and . These graphs all illustrate the unemployment rate—but from different perspectives.
p239.zh: 图表不仅揭示了规律,而且还可以改变对规律的看法。 要看到一些可以做到的方法,请考虑[,]的行图,和. 这些图表都说明了失业率,但从不同角度来说。

p240.original: Presenting Unemployment Rates in Different Ways, All of Them Accurate
p240.zh: 以不同方式呈现失业率,所有准确度

p241.original: Presenting Unemployment Rates in Different Ways, All of Them Accurate
p241.zh: 以不同方式呈现失业率,所有准确度

p242.original: Suppose you wanted a graph which gives the impression that the rise in unemployment in 2009 was not all that large, or all that extraordinary by historical standards. You might choose to present your data as in  (a).  (a) includes much of the same data presented earlier in , but stretches the horizontal axis out longer relative to the vertical axis. By spreading the graph wide and flat, the visual appearance is that the rise in unemployment is not so large, and is similar to some past rises in unemployment. Now imagine you wanted to emphasize how unemployment spiked substantially higher in 2009. In this case, using the same data, you can stretch the vertical axis out relative to the horizontal axis, as in  (b), which makes all rises and falls in unemployment appear larger.
p242.zh: 假设你想要一张图表 给人以2009年失业率上升的印象 并不是那么大,或者说从历史标准来看 如此非凡。 您可以选择以(a)段的形式显示您的数据。(a) 包括早先在......中提出的大部分相同数据,但相对垂直轴将水平轴拉长。 通过将图表广度和平度的分布,视觉外观显示失业率的上升并不大,与过去一些失业率的上升类似. 现在想象一下,你想强调2009年失业率的飙升。 在这种情况下,使用同样的数据,可以将垂直轴线与水平轴线相对的伸展,如(b)中,这使得所有失业率的上升和下降都显得更大。

p243.original: A similar effect can be accomplished without changing the length of the axes, but by changing the scale on the vertical axis. In  (c), the scale on the vertical axis runs from 0% to 30%, while in  (d), the vertical axis runs from 3% to 10%. Compared to , where the vertical scale runs from 0% to 12%,  (c) makes the fluctuation in unemployment look smaller, while  (d) makes it look larger.
p243.zh: 在不改变轴线长度的情况下,可以通过改变垂直轴线上的尺度来实现类似的效果. 在(c)中,垂直轴上的比分从0%到30%,而在(d)中,垂直轴的比分从3%到10%。与垂直比例从0%到12%相比,(c) 失业率的波动较小,(d) 失业率较大。

p244.original: Another way to alter the perception of the graph is to reduce the amount of variation by changing the number of points plotted on the graph.  (e) shows the unemployment rate according to five-year averages. By averaging out some of the year-to-year changes, the line appears smoother and with fewer highs and lows. In reality, the unemployment rate is reported monthly, and  (f) shows the monthly figures since 1960, which fluctuate more than the five-year average.  (f) is also a vivid illustration of how graphs can compress lots of data. The graph includes monthly data since 1960, which over almost 50 years, works out to nearly 600 data points. Reading that list of 600 data points in numerical form would be hypnotic. You can, however, get a good intuitive sense of these 600 data points very quickly from the graph.
p244.zh: 另一种改变图的感知的方法是通过改变图上绘图的点数来减少变数.(e) 按五年平均数显示失业率。 通过年与年之间的一些变化的平均值,线路显得较为平滑,且高低较少. 实际上,失业率每月报告一次,(f) 显示自1960年以来的每月数字,该数字波动超过五年平均数。(f) 也是图表如何压缩大量数据的生动说明。 该图包括自1960年以来的月度数据,在近50年的时间里,数据达到近600个数据点.以数字形式阅读600个数据点的清单将是催眠的。 然而,你可以很快地从图中 得到一个很好的直观感,来了解这600个数据点。

p245.original: A final trick in manipulating the perception of graphical information is that, by choosing the starting and ending points carefully, you can influence the perception of whether the variable is rising or falling. The original data show a general pattern with unemployment low in the 1960s, but spiking up in the mid-1970s, early 1980s, early 1990s, early 2000s, and late 2000s.  (g), however, shows a graph that goes back only to 1975, which gives an impression that unemployment was more-or-less gradually falling over time until the 2009 recession pushed it back up to its “original” level—which is a plausible interpretation if one starts at the high point around 1975.
p245.zh: 操纵图形信息感知的最后一种技巧是,通过仔细选择起始点和结束点,可以影响对变量是上升还是下降的感知.原始数据显示了1960年代失业率低的一般模式,但在1970年代中期、1980年代初、1990年代初、2000年代初和2000年代末,失业率上升。 然而,图表显示的只是1975年,这给人一种印象,即失业在一段时间后逐渐下降,直到2009年经济衰退将其推回“原始”水平,如果从1975年左右的高峰开始,这种解释是可信的。

p246.original: These kinds of tricks—or shall we just call them “presentation choices”— are not limited to line graphs. In a pie chart with many small slices and one large slice, someone must decide what categories should be used to produce these slices in the first place, thus making some slices appear bigger than others. If you are making a bar graph, you can make the vertical axis either taller or shorter, which will tend to make variations in the height of the bars appear more or less.
p246.zh: 这些诡计——或者我们只是称之为“介绍选择”——并不限于行图。 在一张带有许多小片和大片的馅饼图中,人们必须先决定用什么类别来生产这些切片,从而使一些切片显得比其他切片更大. 如果您正在制作一个条形图,您可以使垂直轴高一些或短一些,这往往会使条形的高度变化多多少少。

p247.original: Being able to read graphs is an essential skill, both in economics and in life. A graph is just one perspective or point of view, shaped by choices such as those discussed in this section. Do not always believe the first quick impression from a graph. View with caution.
p247.zh: 能够读懂图表是经济学和生活的基本技能。图表只是一种观点或观点,由本节所讨论的选择所决定。 不要总是相信从图表上得出的第一快印象。仔细观察。

p249.original: Math is a tool for understanding economics and economic relationships can be expressed mathematically using algebra or graphs. The algebraic equation for a line is y = b + mx, where x is the variable on the horizontal axis and y is the variable on the vertical axis, the b term is the y-intercept and the m term is the slope. The slope of a line is the same at any point on the line and it indicates the relationship (positive, negative, or zero) between two economic variables.
p249.zh: 数学是理解经济学和经济学关系的工具,可以用代数或图表在数学上表达. 一行的代数方程为y=b + mx,其中x是水平轴上的变量,y是垂直轴上的变量,b术语为y-intercept,m术语为斜面.一条线的坡度在线上的任意一点都是一样的,它表明两个经济变量之间的关系(正,负,或零).

p250.original: Economic models can be solved algebraically or graphically. Graphs allow you to illustrate data visually. They can illustrate patterns, comparisons, trends, and apportionment by condensing the numerical data and providing an intuitive sense of relationships in the data. A line graph shows the relationship between two variables: one is shown on the horizontal axis and one on the vertical axis. A pie graph shows how something is allotted, such as a sum of money or a group of people. The size of each slice of the pie is drawn to represent the corresponding percentage of the whole. A bar graph uses the height of bars to show a relationship, where each bar represents a certain entity, like a country or a group of people. The bars on a bar graph can also be divided into segments to show subgroups.
p250.zh: 经济模型可以通过代数或图形解析.图表允许您以视觉方式显示数据。 它们可以通过对数字数据进行压缩,在数据中提供直观的关系感来说明规律、比较、趋势和分配。 一个行图显示了两个变量之间的关系:一个在水平轴上显示,一个在垂直轴上显示. 一个派图显示什么是分配的,比如一笔钱或一群人. 每片馅饼的大小被绘制出来,以表示整个饼饼的相应百分比. 一个条形图利用条形的高度来显示一种关系,其中每个条形代表某个实体,比如一个国家或一群人.条形图上的条也可以被分为段以显示分组.

p251.original: Any graph is a single visual perspective on a subject. The impression it leaves will be based on many choices, such as what data or time frame is included, how data or groups are divided up, the relative size of vertical and horizontal axes, whether the scale used on a vertical starts at zero. Thus, any graph should be regarded somewhat skeptically, remembering that the underlying relationship can be open to different interpretations.
p251.zh: 任何图表都是对一个主题的单一视觉视角. 它留下的印象将基于许多选择,例如包含哪些数据或时间框架,数据或组是如何划分的,垂直轴和水平轴的相对大小,垂直上使用的尺度是否从零开始. 因此,任何图表都应在某种程度上被怀疑,要记住根本的关系可以有不同的解释。

p253.original: Name three kinds of graphs and briefly state when is most appropriate to use each type of graph.
p253.zh: 命名三种图表,并简要说明最适合使用每一种图表的时间。

p254.original: What is slope on a line graph?
p254.zh: 线条图上的斜度是什么?

p256.original: Why is a bar chart the best way to illustrate comparisons?
p256.zh: 为什么条形图是说明比较的最佳方法?

p257.zh: 正坡的外观与负坡和零坡有何不同?

c1.original: This line graph has x on the horizontal axis and y on the vertical axis. The y-intercept—that is, the point where the line intersects the y-axis—is 9. The slope of the line is 3; that is, there is a rise of 3 on the vertical axis for every increase of 1 on the horizontal axis. The slope is the same all along a straight line.
c1.zh: 此行图在水平轴上有x,在垂直轴上有y.y - 接合点—— 即线条交叉的y - 轴点—— 是 9。线路的坡度为3;也就是说,纵轴上每增加1个横向轴时,均会上升3个.斜坡沿直线完全相同.

c2.original: The equations for Qd and Qs are displayed graphically by the sloped lines.
c2.zh: Qd和Q的方程式用斜线图形显示.

c3.original: The line graph shows the relationship between height and weight for boys and girls from birth to 3 years. Point A, for example, shows that a boy of 28 inches in height (measured on the horizontal axis) is typically 19 pounds in weight (measured on the vertical axis). These data apply only to children in the first three years of life.
c3.zh: 线形图显示了男孩和女孩从出生到3岁时的身高和体重之间的关系. 例如,A点显示一个身高28英寸(测量在水平轴上)的男孩一般是体重19磅(测量在垂直轴上).这些数据只适用于生命的头三年的儿童。

c4.original: This line graph shows the relationship between altitude, measured in meters above sea level, and air density, measured in kilograms of air per cubic meter. As altitude rises, air density declines. The point at the top of Mount Everest has an altitude of approximately 8,828 meters above sea level (the horizontal axis) and air density of 0.023 kilograms per cubic meter (the vertical axis).
c4.zh: 本行图显示海拔高度(海拔米数)与空气密度(每立方公尺空气公斤数)之间的关系. 随着高度的上升,空气密度下降.珠穆朗玛峰顶部的海拔高度约为8,828米(水平轴),空气密度为0.023公斤每立方公尺(垂直轴).

c6.original: This graph provides a quick visual summary of unemployment data. With a graph like this, it is easy to spot the times of high unemployment and of low unemployment.
c6.zh: 该图提供了失业数据的快速视觉摘要。有了这样的图表,就很容易发现高失业率和低失业率的时代。

c8.original: The three pie graphs illustrate the division of total population into three age groups for the three different years.
c8.zh: 三个派图说明了总人口在三年不同的年龄划分为三个年龄组的情况.

c9.original: The graph shows the 12 countries of the world with the largest populations. The height of the bars in the bar graph shows the size of the population for each country.
c9.zh: 该图显示了世界上人口最多的12个国家.条形图中的条形高度显示了每个国家的人口规模.

c10.original: Population data can be represented in different ways. (a) Shows three bars for each year, representing the total number of persons in each age bracket for each year. (b) Shows just one bar for each year, but the different age groups are now shaded inside the bar. (c) Sets the vertical axis as a measure of percentages rather than the number of persons. All three bar graphs are the same height and each bar is divided according to the percentage of population in each age group.
c10.zh: 人口数据可以用不同方式反映。(a) 每年显示三个栏,代表每年每个年龄段的总人数。(b) 每年只显示一个栏目,但不同年龄组现在在栏目内有阴影。(c) 确定垂直轴线,作为衡量百分比而不是人数的尺度。 所有三个条形图的高度都相同,每个条形图都按照每个年龄组的人口百分比进行划分.

c11.original: Simply changing the width and height of the area in which data is displayed can alter the perception of the data.
c11.zh: 仅仅改变数据显示区域的宽度和高度就可以改变对数据的认知。

c12.original: Simply changing the width and height of the area in which data is displayed can alter the perception of the data.
c12.zh: 仅仅改变数据显示区域的宽度和高度就可以改变对数据的认知。
